full_judgment:
The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that 'A' schedule land to the plaint belonged to Gopal Mondal who died leaving behind two daughters namely, Maharani Mondal and Sachi Rani: Maharani Mondal died leaving behind one son, Gurudas Sarker. During SA operation, the suit land was recorded in the names of Gurudas Sarker and Debendra Mondal in SA khatian No. 155 in CS and SA Plot No. 78, measuring an area of land 1.16 acres. After that, SA recorded tenant, Debendra Mondal died leaving behind only son, Bireshwar Mondal (defendant No. 1) who had been in exclusive possession in his portion of the suit plot No. 78. He appointed Md. Shahidullah (defendant No. 2) as his constituted attorney by a registered power of attorney dated 04-5-1999 to protect, preserve, sell or otherwise dispose of the suit land on his behalf. On 27-9-1999, corresponding to 12th Aswin,1406 BS, defendant No. 2 executed and registered an agreement for sale of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs on receipt of Tk. 3,00,000 as earnest money out of total consideration of Tk. 16,50,000. It was stipulated between the parties that the deed of sale would be executed and registered within 30-6-2000 on receipt of the balance consideration money. It is also stipulated that the concerned office of the Sub-Registrar would not deliver the original deed of power of attorney and the deed of agreement till that time. Therefore, the plaintiffs filed true copy of the said agreement along with receipts of those documents. Defendant No.2 received a further sum of Tk. 7,00,000 on 20-10-1999 and Tk. 6,25,000 on 25-11-1999 on granting proper acknowledge receipts and thus defendants received a total sum of Tk. 16,25,000. On 25-11-1999, the plaintiffs tendered the balance consideration money of Tk. 25,000 to defendant No. 2. After that, on several occasions, they tendered the balance consideration money and requested defendant No. 2 to execute and register the deed of sale in respect of 'B' schedule land in favour of the plaintiffs. But defendant No. 2 on different pleas did not do so. On 30-6-2000 defendant No. 2 refused to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiffs. Hence, the plaintiffs had to file the suit for specific performance of contract in respect of the land described in the schedule 'B' to the plaint. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 4-9 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that Gopal Mondal was the owner of the suit land of CS khatian No. 114 in CS Plot No. 78 measuring an area of 1.06 acres of land. During SA operation 1.16 acres of land of plot No. 78 were recorded in the name of Gurudas Mistiri. While in possession of the suit land, Gurudas Mistri gifted 0.60 acre of land out of 1.16 acres of land to his sister Srimoti Sudhamoni by a registered deed dated 23-1-1947. After that, Sudhamoni transferred her share in favour of Ahmed Hossain and Nur Mohammad by a registered deed dated 01-5-1950. Meanwhile, the Government acquired 7 decimals of land from suit plot No. 78 pursuant to LA Case No. 13/1967-1968 for construction of Dhaka-Narayangonj Link Road and remaining 51 decimals of land were in possession of Ahmed Hossain and Nur Mohammad. During RS operation, the said land was recorded in their names in RS khatian No. 173 in Plot No. 256. After that, Nur Mohammad gifted his share in the suit plot to his wife, Kewrar Bibi by a registered deed of gift dated 24-4-1980. While jointly possessing 0.51 acre of land, Ahmed Hossain and Kewrar Bibi transferred the same to defendant Nos.4-8 by five registered deeds of sale dated 15-11-1982 and one Shamsul Haque by a registered deed dated 15-12-1982 delivered possession of the suit land to them. After that, Shamsul Haque transferred his 8½ decimals of land to one Fatema Akther by a registered deed dated 29-7-1993. Subsequently, Fatema Akther transferred the same to defendant No. 9 by a registered deed dated 26-4-1995 and defendant Nos. 4-9 mutated their names in respect of their purchased land and had since been paying rent regularly. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are land grabbers and defendant No. 1 fraudulently created a registered power of attorney in respect of 58 decimals land out of the total land of CS Plot No. 78 and appointed defendant No. 2 as his attorney. On the strength of said forged power of attorney, the defendants in collusion with some miscreants had been trying to take forcible possession of the suit land from defendant Nos. 4-9. In such a situation, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 168 of 1999 against defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for permanent injunction. In the meantime, defendant No. 1 cancel-led the power of attorney by a registered deed dated 20-1-2000 and the plaintiffs did not get possession of the suit land on the basis of agreement dated 27-7-1999 and the suit being false is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Senior Advocates, the impugned judgment and the materials on record. Admittedly, the suit land originally belonged to Gopal Mondal. From SA khatian No.155 (exhibit-2), it appears that Debandra Mondal, father of defendant No. 1., was a recorded tenant. While in possession of the land of suit plot No. 78, defendant No. 1 appointed defendant No. 2 as his attorney to manage, sell and dispose of the suit land. The power of attorney has been filed and marked as Exhibit-3. According to the plaintiffs, defendant No. 2 as the constituted attorney of defendant No.1 entered into a contract with the plaintiffs to sell the suit land for a consideration of Tk.16,50,000 by a registered deed of agreement dated 27-9-1999. On the date of execution of the agreement, defendant No. 2 was stated to have received Tk.300,000 as earnest money and subsequently, the plaintiffs paid different amounts to defendant No. 2 on proper receipts. All told, the plaintiffs stated to have paid Tk. 16, 25,000 to defendant No. 2. Accordingly, the plaintiffs tendered the balance consideration of money amounting to Tk. 25000 to defendant No. 2 and requested him to execute and register the deed of sale but the defendants refused to do so.
